"FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Mosquito mats containing allethrin when healed on electrical beaters specially designed for the purpose will emit vapour of allethrin. The mosquito mats are generally manufactured to contain allethrin 4.0 percent (min,) (d-isolner 95 percent, minimum (mlm�). The Registration Conuuinee constituted under the Insecticides Act,1968 by tbe Govcnuncnt of India, has granted registration to mosquito nt818 containing allethrin as an active ingrdient, after examining the toxicity data submitted by tbe applicant and satisfying itself that the product is safe to human beings if used as prescribed, In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to tbe provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and tbe Rules framed tbereunder. However, the standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these wberever applicable, For til", purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of tbis standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance witb IS 2:1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should he the sante as tbat of the specified value in this sift ndard.'

FOREWORD
This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides Sectional Committee had been approved by the Pood and Agriculture Division Council. Mosquito mats containing allethrin when heated on electrical heaters specially designed for the purpose will emit vapour of allethrin. The mosquito mats are generally manufactured ( d-isomer 9S percent, minimum ( "'/111 ) l. to contain allethrin 4�0 percent ( mlm v

In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Rules frame thereunder. However, the standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of U test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 "Rules for rounding off numer'ical values i revlsed )'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX A

( Clauses 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 )
DETERMINATION OF ALLETHRIN AND PIPERONYL BIJTOXIDE CONTENTS A-I GENERAL Both allethrin and piperonyl butoxide are extracted from the mat using toluene as solvent and estimated gas chromatographically using a hydrogen flame ionization detector. A-2 APPARATUS A-Z.I Gas Cbromatograph Equlpped with a hydrogen flame ionization detector and may be coupled to an integrator cum printer-plotter. Any gas chromatograph can be used with the following operating conditions, which may be varied subject to sta ndard j za t ion: A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution

Weigh accurately 0�04 g of dibutyl phthalate into a clean 100-mJ volumetric flask and made up the volume to 100 ml with toluene. 1 ml the resultant solution will contain 4 mg of dibutyl phthalate. This will be used as a stock

or

solution.

A-4.Z Preparation of Allethrin Standard Solution Weigh accurately 0�04 g of allethrin reference standard into a clean IOO-ml volumetric ilask and dissolve the material using about 40-50 ml of toluene. Add exactlv 10 ml of internal standard solution and then make up the volume to 100 ml with toluene. 1 ml of the resultant solution will contain 0�4 mg of allethrin and 0�4 mg of dibutyl phthalate. A-4.3 Preparation of Piperooyl Butoxide Staadard Solution Weigh accurately 0�01 mg ofpiperonyl butoxide ( PDO ) reference standard into a clean lOO-ml volumetric flask and dissolve the material using about 40-50 ml of toluene. Add exactly 10 ml of internal standard solution and then make up the volume to 100 ml with toluene. 1 ml of the resultant solution will contain 0�10 mg of PDO and 0�4 mg of dibutyl phthalate. A-4.4 Extraction from the Mat aDd Preparation of Sample Solutioo A-4.4.1 Weigh accurately about 1�0 g of finely cut mat pieces and transfer into a 12S-ml stoppered conical flask. Add approximately 60 mt toluene and shake thoroughly for 20 minutes on a mechanical, shaker. Carefully transfer the supernatant liquid into a clean lOO-ml volumetric flask. Wash the contents of the conical flask twice with 10 ml portions of toluene, adding the washings to the volumetric flask. Add exactly 10 ml of internal standard solution and make up the volume to 100 ml with toluene. Mix well. A-4.5 Estimation

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau ofIndian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmoniou~ development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods� and attending to. connected matters in the country. "
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'SIS Catalogue' and 'Standards: Monthly Additions'.
